stops.title: Conductivity, molar conductivity & Kohlrausch law
stops.inShort: Molar conductivity Λ = 1000 κ / c (SI unit: S·m²·mol⁻¹ or Ω⁻¹·cm²·mol⁻¹). Kohlrausch law: Λ₀ = n₊ λ°₊ + n₋ λ°₋. Degree of dissociation α = Λ / Λ₀.

stops.title: Electrolysis & Faraday's laws
stops.inShort: Faraday's 1st law: mass deposited W = Q·M / (n·F) = I·t·M / (n·F), where 1 F = 96500 C/mol.

stops.title: Galvanic cell, Nernst equation & Gibbs energy
stops.inShort: E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode. Nernst equation at 298 K: E_cell = E°_cell − (0.0592/n) log₁₀ Q. Thermodynamics: ΔG° = −n F E°_cell.

stops.title: Reference electrode (SHE), Batteries, Fuel cell & Electrochemical series
stops.inShort: SHE: E° = 0.00 V. Lead accumulator discharging net reaction: Pb + PbO₂ + 2H₂SO₄ → 2PbSO₄ + 2H₂O. H₂-O₂ fuel cell converts chemical energy directly to electricity. Electrochemical series lists E°_red values.

board.text: The formula used to calculate molar conductivity of an electrolyte is ____.
How many coulombs of electricity is required to produce 1 g of sodium metal by reduction of sodium ion?
board.answer:
Na⁺ + e⁻ → Na (n = 1, M = 23 g/mol).
23 g Na requires 1 F = 96500 C.
1 g Na requires Q = 96500 / 23 = 4195.65 C.

points.text: 1 mol Na (23 g) requires 1 F = 96500 C

board.text: Draw a neat and labelled diagram of a lead accumulator cell. Write the overall reactions taking place at cathode and anode during discharging of the cell.
board.answer:
Diagram: Lead grids packed with spongy Pb (anode) and PbO₂ (cathode) immersed in 38% H₂SO₄ (density 1.2 g/mL).
Anode (oxidation): Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻
Cathode (reduction): PbO₂(s) + 4H⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l)
Net reaction: Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) → 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l).

points.text: Neat labelled diagram (Pb anode, PbO₂ cathode, H₂SO₄)

board.text: Write SI unit of molar conductivity.
Calculate the time required to deposit 2.4 g of Cu, when 2.03 A of current passed through CuSO₄ solution. (At. mass of Cu = 63.5 g·mol⁻¹)
Define electrochemical series and write its two applications.
board.answer:
Electrochemical series: The arrangement of electrodes (half-cells) in the order of their decreasing standard reduction potentials (E°).
Applications:
1. Relative strength of oxidizing and reducing agents (higher E° = stronger oxidizing agent).
2. Predicting spontaneity of redox reactions (E°_cell = E°_cathode − E°_anode > 0 is spontaneous).
